target.executionProfile: local Prefect API server; 127.0.0.1:4200/api; one API server worker with SQLite; UI and scheduler disabled; ThreadPoolTaskRunner(max_workers=4) at Root, Stage and Step Flow levels. API-server worker count and client task-runner thread count are separate settings.

topology.invocationMechanism: Two Prefect dispatch Tasks are submitted. Each dispatch Task invokes a distinct Stage-specific Flow object created with Flow.with_options(name=...).
topology.nativeEvidence: One Root Flow Run; two Stage Flow Runs; each child Stage Flow has a native parent_task_run_id.
topology.semanticRule: Root owns inclusion and invocation of Stage Parent Flows; Prefect performs orchestration. Dispatch Tasks do not become GPWCF semantic components.

topology.prefectConstruct: Native Prefect Flow / Stage Parent Flow
topology.invocationMechanism: invoke_stage dispatch Task invokes the Stage-specific Flow object. Stage submits Step dispatch Tasks; each dispatch invokes the Step public callable.
topology.nativeEvidence: Each Stage is a distinct native Flow Run correlated to the Root Flow Run and native dispatch Task Run.
topology.semanticRule: Stage controls its Step membership and Stage-specific composition. It does not call SPU Tasks directly.

topology.invocationMechanism: StepFacade.execute(input) is the Stage-facing public callable. It invokes a Step-specific Flow object created with Flow.with_options(name=...).
topology.nativeEvidence: Each Step is a distinct native Flow Run correlated to its owning Stage Flow and native dispatch Task Run.
topology.semanticRule: The Step public callable is the only Stage-facing entry into the Step. SPU invocation and Step result assembly remain inside the Step Subflow.

topology.invocationMechanism: The Step Flow submits both SPU Tasks to its ThreadPoolTaskRunner and joins their futures.
topology.nativeEvidence: Each SPU has an independently observable native Task Run ID; both SPU tasks completed for every tested Step invocation.
topology.semanticRule: SPUs execute inside the owning Step Subflow. SPUExecutionResult remains distinct from StepExecutionResult.

dispatchMechanismDecision.reason: Prefect 3.9.2 Flow objects do not expose a submit method; Task objects do. The PoC therefore uses narrow Prefect Task dispatch wrappers to invoke native child Flow objects while preserving Prefect parent_task_run_id relationships.
constraints: Dispatch wrappers carry no GPWCF business or composition semantics.
They do not select SPUs, implement Step Composition, or assemble domain results.
The public StepFacade.execute method remains the only Stage-facing Step entry point.

flowIdentityDecision.mechanism: Flow.with_options(name=...) creates a Stage- or Step-specific named Flow object at the target integration boundary.
flowIdentityDecision.rationale: Distinct Stage/Step specializations remain separately identifiable in Prefect native Flow Run records.
flowIdentityDecision.boundary: The Prefect Flow name is an operational label, not a replacement for GPWCF domain identity or invocation identity.

repeatedRuns.profile: local-prefect-server-api-sqlite-single-worker; run script using external Prefect home

aggregate.stepSiblingSubflowOverlap: 0/8 Stage sibling pairs; serialized in all four runs

concurrencyFindings.disposition: The native Root/Stage/Step hierarchy is executable and parent-correlated. However, Root-to-Stage sibling Flow overlap occurred in only three of four repeated runs, so it is not guaranteed. Stage-to-Step sibling Subflows were serialized in all eight observed pairs. Step-internal SPU Task fan-out/fan-in overlapped in every tested Step invocation.
concurrencyFindings.serverConstraint: Prefect rejects API-server multi-worker mode when SQLite is the database. Multi-worker API-server mode requires PostgreSQL. This qualification uses the supported single-worker SQLite server profile; ThreadPoolTaskRunner(max_workers=4) is a separate client-side setting.
concurrencyFindings.designConsequence: Do not assume independent Generator Stages can execute concurrently merely because Root submits multiple dispatch Tasks. If a Generator scenario requires concurrent Stage Parent Flows, qualify an alternative Prefect-native dispatch/execution profile that preserves Stage Flow identity and explicit parent correlation. Apply the same rule to sibling Step Subflows only where the concrete Step Composition requires it.

resultAndIdentityDecision.operationalState: Prefect State is captured in separate operational evidence and is not embedded in pipeline-result.json.
resultAndIdentityDecision.identitySeparation: GPWCF domain identities and invocation identities are recorded separately from Prefect Flow Run IDs and Task Run IDs.
resultAndIdentityDecision.errorProbe: A controlled RuntimeError caused the probe Task to enter FAILED while the probe Flow returned COMPLETED after catching the exception. No GPWCF domain structured result was fabricated.

nextRequiredWork: Retain the qualified native hierarchy boundary mapping as the candidate integration shape.
Investigate and qualify a deterministic Prefect-native mechanism for concurrent sibling Stage Flow runs while preserving native Flow identity and Root-to-Stage correlation.
Determine whether actual Generator Stage specializations require sibling Step Subflow concurrency; current evidence shows sibling Step Subflows serialized in the local SQLite profile.
If multi-worker Prefect API-server execution is considered, first qualify the PostgreSQL-backed server profile and its dependency/operations implications.
Do not begin production Stage mapping that assumes sibling Stage parallelism until the concurrency gap is resolved.
